title: Speech capabilities and user benefits · Level 1
slo: Explain what speech recognition and speech synthesis do and how they support users.

exercises.question_text: What does speech recognition do? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Recognition takes spoken language as input. It begins with captured speech.
Producing written text from speech is recognition's core role. It is therefore called speech-to-text.
A transcription gives an app usable written content. That supports understanding a spoken request.
Reading text aloud is speech synthesis. Recognition moves from speech to text instead.

feedback.intrinsic: No written transcript would be produced.
feedback.instructional: Recognition listens and writes; synthesis speaks.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition listens to speech and produces text.

exercises.question_text: What does accessibility mean in a speech-enabled experience?

options.rationale: Accessibility considers people with different abilities and needs. It aims to prevent barriers to use.

options.text: Using one voice for all users
options.rationale: A consistent voice may support branding. It does not address different access needs.
options.better_fit: It fits a consistent brand-voice decision.

feedback.intrinsic: Users could still face access barriers.
feedback.instructional: Accessibility provides usable choices for different needs.

options.rationale: Speech-only input can exclude people who need another method. Accessible applications also provide text alternatives.
options.better_fit: It fits hands-free use for a person who chooses to speak.

feedback.intrinsic: Some users could not use the experience.
feedback.instructional: Accessibility means offering alternatives, not requiring speech.

options.rationale: Sampling rate affects audio detail. It does not by itself remove access barriers.

feedback.intrinsic: Clearer audio would not supply text access.
feedback.instructional: Accessibility concerns user needs and alternative methods.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Accessibility designs for different user needs.

exercises.question_text: Speech recognition is useful when an application must understand what a person says.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would overlook recognition's purpose in a voice interface.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Applications use recognition to turn what people say into usable written text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition makes spoken requests available as text.

exercises.question_text: When speech is available, an application no longer needs text-based input and output alternatives.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This could leave some users without access.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Some users prefer or require non-speech interfaces, so provide text input and output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech does not remove the need for text alternatives.

exercises.question_text: Which are benefits of speech-enabled experiences? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Speech can reduce reliance on keyboards and screens. This enables hands-free operation.
Speech can be used while another task continues. This supports multitasking.
Speaking and hearing can feel conversational. This can make interactions more natural.
Speech does not eliminate the need for text alternatives. Some users prefer or require non-speech access.
options.better_fit: Speech-only interaction may fit a limited context, but not accessible general design.

feedback.intrinsic: Users needing text could lose access.
feedback.instructional: Speech expands choices; it should not remove text alternatives.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech can support hands-free work, multitasking, and natural interaction.

options.rationale: Speech capabilities work with spoken language. Recognition and synthesis handle its input or output.
Written text can feed synthesis, but it is not the whole scope. Speech capabilities also handle spoken input or output.
options.better_fit: Written text is the input for speech synthesis.

feedback.intrinsic: This would leave out spoken input.
feedback.instructional: Speech capabilities concern spoken language through recognition and synthesis.

options.rationale: Storing audio does not understand or generate language. It is distinct from speech conversion.
options.better_fit: Audio storage is useful for retaining recordings.

feedback.intrinsic: A recording alone would not create a transcript or reply.
feedback.instructional: Recognition and synthesis perform the language conversions.

options.rationale: Phoneme probabilities can occur inside recognition. They do not describe the complete speech capability.

feedback.intrinsic: This omits usable text and spoken output.
feedback.instructional: Speech capabilities are broader than one internal recognition signal.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Speech capabilities work with spoken language.

exercises.question_text: Using recognition and synthesis together can enable hands-free operation and support multitasking.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This overlooks a practical benefit of voice interaction.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Recognition handles spoken input and synthesis provides spoken output.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Two-way voice interaction can reduce reliance on keyboards and screens.

exercises.question_text: Speech recognition converts written text into spoken audio.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Recognition is speech-to-text; synthesis is text-to-speech.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That conversion is speech synthesis.

exercises.question_text: Which name also refers to speech synthesis?

options.rationale: Text-to-speech is another name for speech synthesis. Both convert written text into spoken audio.
Speech-to-text converts speech into written text. That process is speech recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: A written notice would not be spoken.

options.rationale: Audio capture records incoming sound. It does not generate spoken audio from text.
options.better_fit: It fits the first step of recognition.

options.rationale: Language modeling helps select likely word sequences. It is not the text-to-audio capability.

feedback.instructional: Use synthesis when text must be spoken aloud.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with speech experiences, then state the benefits.

exercises.correct_answer: Speech experiences can support hands-free operation and multitasking
exercises.explanation: Speech experiences can support hands-free work and multitasking.

exercises.question_text: Speech capabilities include speech recognition and ___, which speaks written text aloud.

parts.text: Speech capabilities include speech recognition and

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The missing term would not name the spoken-output capability.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use speech synthesis for text becoming speech.

exercises.explanation: Speech synthesis, also called text-to-speech or TTS, converts text into spoken audio.

exercises.question_text: Speech synthesis listens to spoken language and converts it into written text.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Synthesis starts with text and produces spoken audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. That description belongs to speech recognition.

flashcards.back: It converts spoken language into written text.
It converts written text into natural-sounding spoken audio.

flashcards.front: What benefit enables use without hands?
What should speech apps always provide?
